subject.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)

question: Should completed nonzero exec results be treated as identical regardless of output and intervening exec progress, or should the breaker preserve a progress signal for legitimate polling workflows?
rationale: Both choices are defensible safety policies: unconditional collapsing stops costly runaway retries sooner, while preserving interleaved or meaningful progress avoids false-positive session blocks; code inspection alone cannot establish the intended product tradeoff.

options.title: Preserve interleaved progress
options.body: Count stable repeated failures, but reset the streak when intervening exec activity or a supported normalized progress signal shows forward movement, with tests for both paths.

options.title: Fail closed on nonzero
options.body: Keep every same-command completed nonzero outcome output-insensitive and explicitly accept and document the false-positive blocking risk for polling-style workflows.

recommendation.title: Preserve interleaved progress
recommendation.body: Count stable repeated failures, but reset the streak when intervening exec activity or a supported normalized progress signal shows forward movement, with tests for both paths.
